newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile has 2 yrs to change environment rules - Canada.
newsitem.headline: Chile has 2 yrs to change environment rules - Canada.

text.p: Canada will give Chile two years to make improvements in its environmental rules as required by a free trade agreement between the two countries, said Canadian Environment Minister Sergio Marchi on Monday.

"Chile must define standards of air, water and soil quality, develop ways of making sure rules are met and make it obligatory to evaluate a project's environmental impact," Marchi told newspaper El Mercurio.
The new standards must be met not only by the government, but also by private companies, he said.
The two-year period will start when the treaty comes into force, probably in June 1997, said Marchi.

The free trade agreement with Canada is the first agreement Chile has signed including environment and labor conditions and is expected to form the basis for the country's much-delayed entry into the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
Chile was invited in 1994 to join NAFTA, which groups Canada, the United States and Mexico, but talks stalled due to political difficulties in Washington.
Last month, President Eduardo Frei and Canadian leader Jean Chretien signed a protocol of the agreement, which will sweep away tariffs on 80 percent of bilateral trade as soon as it comes into force.
The final accord will be signed in Santiago this week by Canada's International Trade Minister Art Eggleton and Chilean Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
Canada is one of the top foreign investors in Chile with Canadian businessmen investing billions of dollars in the country's booming mining industry.
